evidence.explanation: General hearing habilitation guidance, not a genotype-specific efficacy estimate.

treatments/1.description: Consider cochlear implantation according to audiologic candidacy, benefit from amplification, anatomy and family goals. It supports auditory access without correcting GJB2. The reviewed sources do not establish that every DFNA3A patient has an intact auditory nerve or uniformly good implant outcomes.

evidence.snippet: In a transgenic mouse model with the GJB2 R75W mutation, AAV-mediated base editing also restored the fragmented GJPs to orderly outlines in cochlear supporting cells.
evidence.explanation: Plaque morphology is structural evidence; channel function was tested in HeLa cells, not directly in the treated cochlea.

evidence.snippet: Larger and longer experiments are required to assess improvement of hearing loss and currently evaluating the therapeutic efficacy to auditory function by AAV-mediated base editing.
evidence.explanation: The authors explicitly identify auditory efficacy as requiring further evaluation. Morphologic improvement must not be reported as hearing rescue.

treatments/2.description: Preclinical adenine base editing of p.Arg75Trp restored neurobiotin transfer in an engineered HeLa model and improved gap-junction plaque morphology in mouse cochlear supporting cells. The study used P0 cochlear explants and intracochlear delivery to adult transgenic mice aged 9–30 weeks, with morphology assessed two weeks later. In HeLa cells, 46.8% on-target editing included bystander changes; 28.03% reads were corrected without bystanders. Adult plaque improvement does not establish auditory rescue: baseline ABR characterized the model, but no post-treatment hearing-rescue result was reported. Functional treatment windows, durability, delivery and editing safety remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: In a transgenic mouse model with the GJB2 R75W mutation, AAV-mediated base editing also restored the fragmented GJPs to orderly outlines in cochlear supporting cells.
evidence.explanation: Plaque morphology is structural evidence; channel function was tested in HeLa cells, not directly in the treated cochlea.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Correction of the human p.Arg75Trp transgene improved plaque architecture in supporting cells. This does not demonstrate restored cochlear conductance or hearing.

evidence.snippet: In a mouse model, this siRNA duplex selectively suppressed GJB2(R75W) expression by >70% of control levels, thereby preventing hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Full-paper methods and discussion show acute co-delivery and human–mouse sequence discrimination. This is not established human allele-specific therapy.

evidence.snippet: In vitro treatment with allele-specific small interfering RNA led to robust inhibition of the mutant GJB2 allele without altering expression of the wild-type allele.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates selective knockdown of a mutant GJB2 allele, which is the mechanism this treatment entry proposes. INDIRECT on two counts: the allele is a syndromic one and the cells are keratinocytes, not cochlear.

treatments/3.description: An early proof-of-concept co-delivered human GJB2 p.Arg75Trp plasmid and siRNA to adult mouse round windows, reduced transgene RNA by more than 70% and attenuated the acute ABR threshold shift at 72 hours. Selectivity exploited two human–mouse sequence mismatches; the siRNA also silenced endogenous human GJB2 in cultured cells. This was transient prevention of experimentally induced hearing loss, not reversal of an established inherited lesion or demonstrated mutant-versus-wild-type discrimination in humans. Separately, p.Asp50Asn-selective siRNA improved channel phenotypes in patient-derived KID keratinocytes; that is a different allele and tissue. Durable cochlear delivery, human allele selectivity and safety require further study.

evidence.snippet: Regular follow up is recommended for all individuals with genetic hearing loss
evidence.explanation: General surveillance guidance; frequency should reflect age and observed course.

evidence.snippet: persons with documented hearing loss should be counseled appropriately and repeated overexposure to loud noises should be avoided.
evidence.explanation: General hearing-loss precaution.

treatments/4.description: Follow hearing serially to detect progression and reassess devices and communication needs. Reassess emerging systemic features when indicated. Provide standard noise-protection counseling without assuming special GJB2 susceptibility.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with autosomal dominant hearing loss have a 50% chance of transmitting the pathogenic variant to each child.
evidence.explanation: Applies after establishing a disease-causing dominant allele. Transmission probability does not predict severity, onset or extra-auditory expression.

evidence.snippet: Depending on the specific diagnosis, clinical severity and phenotype may differ between sibs with the same pathogenic variant; thus, age of onset and/or progression cannot be reliably predicted.
evidence.explanation: Do not equate allele transmission with a fixed clinical outcome.

treatments/5.description: Counsel using the specific dominant allele, parental testing and family findings. Discuss 50% transmission from a heterozygous parent separately from variable hearing severity and possible skin involvement. Once the familial variant is established, discuss reproductive testing options with a genetics professional.

hypotheses/0.description: Impaired supporting-cell coupling may disturb cortilymph potassium and contribute to hair-cell injury. Neither cortilymph potassium nor the complete causal sequence was measured directly.

open_questions/0.rationale: Dominant inhibition is demonstrated for p.Trp44Cys and p.Arg75Trp; p.Asp46Asn has segregation evidence without a functional assay in the original report. A historical c.299_300delAT dominant-family observation does not establish a truncation-based dominant mechanism. Syndromic p.Met34Lys trafficking and KID hemichannel results show allelic diversity but cannot be imported as proven DFNA3A routes.

open_questions/1.rationale: Heterologous conductance assays, Gjb6 T5M biochemical-coupling data and p.Arg75Trp transgenic developmental histology describe different systems. None supplies direct human DFNA3A supporting-cell coupling or cortilymph potassium measurements. The 2025 editing study measures functional rescue in HeLa cells and plaque morphology in cochlea, which should be kept distinct.

open_questions/2.rationale: Base editing improved adult mouse plaque morphology but did not report post-treatment auditory rescue. A much earlier siRNA experiment prevented acute plasmid-induced hearing impairment in adult mice. Neither result establishes the timing, durability or reversibility of the inherited developmental lesion. Longitudinal auditory and structural outcomes are needed in clinically relevant allele models.

evidence.snippet: This identified a homozygous splice region variant in STX4 (c.232 + 6T>C), which causes exon skipping and a frameshift, that segregated with HI (two-point logarithm of odds (LOD) score = 5.9).
evidence.explanation: The allele, its molecular consequence, and the evidence that it is the cause.

evidence.snippet: Transgenic overexpression of zebrafish Stx4R241W, analogous to the first patient's STX4R240W variant, indicated that the variant is hypomorphic.
evidence.explanation: Cited for the contrast rather than for DFNB123 itself: the syndromic patients carry a partial-function allele, which is why a frameshift allele producing a different phenotype is not a contradiction. INDIRECT because it is a statement about a different variant in a different species.

steps/1.description:
Homozygosity for a splice-region variant, c.232+6T>C, which causes exon skipping and a consequent frameshift. A frameshift early in the transcript predicts a truncated product or nonsense-mediated decay, so this is treated as a loss-of-function allele; that prediction has not been confirmed by measuring STX4 protein in patient cells.
The missense allele p.Arg240Trp reported in the syndromic STX4 patients is a different kind of change, and its zebrafish equivalent was shown to be hypomorphic rather than null. The two alleles are noted together because the contrast is the most likely explanation for the two different clinical pictures, but they are not pooled: only the splice allele belongs to DFNB123.

evidence.snippet: STX4, a member of the syntaxin family, is a component of the SNARE machinery involved in several vesicle transport and recycling pathways.
evidence.explanation: The molecular identity of the gene product. BACKGROUND because it restates established cell biology rather than reporting this paper's own result.

evidence.snippet: Imaging of Vamp2+ vesicles within stx4 mutant zebrafish hearts showed reduced docking to the cardiomyocyte sarcolemma.
evidence.explanation: The one direct measurement of the fusion defect caused by loss of Stx4 in a vertebrate. INDIRECT because it was made in cardiomyocytes, not hair cells; it establishes that the protein is required for docking, not that this is what fails in the cochlea.

steps/2.description: Syntaxin-4 is a target-SNARE: it sits in the plasma membrane and pairs with vesicle SNAREs to drive the fusion step of vesicle delivery and recycling. Losing it removes one half of that pairing, so vesicles reach the membrane but do not dock and fuse normally. The direct demonstration of that failure is in zebrafish heart, where Vamp2-positive vesicles show reduced docking at the cardiomyocyte sarcolemma in stx4 mutants. Nothing equivalent has been imaged in a hair cell, so the fusion defect is established for the protein and assumed for the ear.

evidence.snippet: In silico analysis showed that murine orthologue Stx4a is highly and widespread expressed in the developing and adult inner ear.
evidence.explanation: The expression argument. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM because the data are mouse, and worth noting that the analysis was in silico over existing expression resources rather than a new measurement.

evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescent imaging revealed localization of STX4A in the cell body, cell membrane and stereocilia of inner and outer hair cells.
evidence.explanation: The subcellular localisation, including the stereocilial pool that links the protein to transduction.

steps/3.description:
The reason a general trafficking protein produces isolated deafness is where it is. The murine orthologue Stx4a is highly and widely expressed through the developing and adult inner ear, and immunofluorescence puts STX4A in three places in both inner and outer hair cells: the cell body, the plasma membrane, and the stereocilia. Stereocilial localisation is the finding that connects a fusion protein to mechanotransduction, because that is where the transduction machinery sits.
Which of the three pools carries the disease-relevant function is not known, and no patient hair cell has been examined.

evidence.snippet: a morpholino-based knockdown of stx4 in zebrafish showed an abnormal startle response, morphological and developmental defects, and a disrupted mechanotransduction function in neuromast hair cells measured via FM1-43 uptake
evidence.explanation: The functional result, its readout, and the behavioural correlate, all from the morpholino knockdown.

evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that STX4 dysfunction leads to HI in humans and zebrafish and supports the evolutionary conserved role of STX4 in inner ear development and hair cell functioning.
evidence.explanation: The conclusion the paper draws, which names both strands of the mechanism this entry curates: development and hair cell function.

steps/4.description:
Knocking down stx4 in zebrafish disrupts mechanotransduction in neuromast hair cells, measured by FM1-43 uptake - the dye enters hair cells through open transduction channels, so reduced uptake reports that the channels are not passing current. The behavioural counterpart in the same animals is an abnormal startle response, which is the whole-animal readout of hair cell function in a larval fish.
This is the node that carries the entity's mechanistic claim, and it is entirely non-mammalian. Neuromast hair cells are lateral-line cells, not cochlear ones, and no mammalian Stx4 hearing model has been reported. The cell type bound here is the human cochlear inner hair cell, because that is what the node is about; the measurement behind it was made in a zebrafish neuromast hair cell, and the gap between the two is the subject of this entry's human-model-mismatch discussion rather than something the binding hides.
The bound process is the detection step rather than the perception it serves. An earlier version bound GO:0050954 sensory perception of mechanical stimulus and GO:0007605 sensory perception of sound, both of which are organism-level processes sitting on a node tagged CELLULAR. GO:0050910 is the cellular transduction event that FM1-43 uptake actually reports, so it matches both the scale tag and the assay.

evidence.snippet: CRISPR/Cas9-generated stx4 mutant zebrafish exhibited defects reminiscent of these patients' clinical presentations, including linearized hearts, bradycardia, otic vesicle dysgenesis, neuronal atrophy, and touch insensitivity by 3 days post fertilization.
evidence.explanation: The otic vesicle phenotype in a genetic null fish, which is the strongest evidence that loss of Stx4 disturbs ear development rather than only ear function. INDIRECT because it comes from the syndromic-STX4 paper and from a fish, so it is two steps from the DFNB123 claim.

steps/5.description: The second strand of the mechanism, and the weaker one. Stx4a is expressed in the developing as well as the adult inner ear, morpholino knockdown produces developmental defects in zebrafish, and CRISPR-generated stx4 mutant fish show frank otic vesicle dysgenesis. Whether anything corresponding happens in a human cochlea is unknown: no imaging of the inner ear is reported for any DFNB123 patient, and severe-to-profound loss with no other feature is compatible with a purely functional lesion.

evidence.snippet: we used exome sequencing to investigate a large consanguineous Pakistani family with eight affected individuals showing bilateral severe-to-profound HI
evidence.explanation: The phenotype, its laterality, its severity range, and the number of affected individuals it was observed in.

steps/6.description: The only feature reported in the DFNB123 family, in all eight affected individuals. The source describes it as bilateral and severe-to-profound. It does not say sensorineural, which is why the bound term is a severity term rather than a sensorineural one; the sensorineural character of STX4-related hearing loss is documented in the separately reported syndromic patient rather than in this family.

evidence.snippet: This identified a homozygous splice region variant in STX4 (c.232 + 6T>C), which causes exon skipping and a frameshift, that segregated with HI (two-point logarithm of odds (LOD) score = 5.9).
evidence.explanation: The causative allele and the segregation evidence for it.

evidence.snippet: A patient with a homozygous R240W missense variant displayed biventricular dilated cardiomyopathy, ectopy, and runs of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, sensorineural hearing loss, global developmental delay, and hypotonia, while a second patient displayed severe pleiotropic abnormalities and perinatal lethality.
evidence.explanation: The other end of the STX4 phenotypic spectrum, recorded here so that a curator reading only the DFNB123 entry is not surprised by a cardiomyopathy report. These patients are not DFNB123 and their features are not curated as phenotypes of it.

genes/0.notes: OMIM records the gene-phenotype relationship as provisional. NCBI mim2gene_medgen maps OMIM:620745 to GeneID 6810 with source GeneMap and the comment `question`, the marker for an OMIM gene-map phenotype carrying a leading question mark. That grading fits the evidence: the segregation within the one reported family is strong, but a single pedigree plus zebrafish and expression data is not multi-family replication.

evidence.snippet: This identified a homozygous splice region variant in STX4 (c.232 + 6T>C), which causes exon skipping and a frameshift, that segregated with HI (two-point logarithm of odds (LOD) score = 5.9).
evidence.explanation: The segregating homozygous allele in a consanguineous pedigree, which is what carrier testing and recurrence counselling act on.

treatments/0.description: Counselling for a recessive condition in a consanguineous family with eight affected members, where the sibling recurrence risk is 25 percent and carrier frequency within the kindred is high. Counselling does not act on the mechanism; it is curated because it is the only intervention the genotype itself indicates.

open_questions/0.rationale:
Two groups have reported biallelic STX4 disease and the pictures do not overlap. The DFNB123 family, homozygous for a splice allele causing exon skipping and a frameshift, has hearing impairment and nothing else in eight affected members. The separately reported patients, one homozygous for the missense allele p.Arg240Trp, have cardiomyopathy with ventricular ectopy, sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay and hypotonia, or perinatal lethality with severe pleiotropic abnormalities. The zebrafish null has both an ear and a heart phenotype, which is what one would expect of a gene used everywhere.
The obvious reading - a dose-dependent allelic series - is complicated by its direction. The zebrafish equivalent of the missense allele is hypomorphic, so the patients with the milder allele have the more severe, multi-system disease, while the family with a frameshift has isolated deafness. That is the wrong way round for a simple dosage model, and it is the reason this is filed as an open question rather than written into the entry as an allelic series. Residual protein from the skipped-exon transcript, modifier background, and ascertainment (a deafness study would not look for subclinical cardiomyopathy) are all live alternatives, and none has been tested.
It matters clinically: if the two are one disease, DFNB123 patients need cardiac surveillance.
One partial answer exists and is recorded here with its provenance, because it cannot be given a verified snippet. The deep-research report committed with this entry reads the full text of the defining paper and states that electrocardiograms were normal in two tested affected relatives of the DFNB123 family, and that no consistent vestibular, facial, neurologic or cardiac abnormality was found. The cached reference for PMID:36355422 is abstract-only, and that sentence is not in the abstract, so no evidence item can carry it. Two normal ECGs in eight affected individuals is in any case a weak negative - it is not echocardiography, and cardiomyopathy in the syndromic patient was dilated rather than electrical - so it narrows the question rather than closing it.

open_questions/1.rationale:
The mechanistic claim in this entry rests on a zebrafish morpholino knockdown assayed in neuromast hair cells. Those are lateral-line cells; a fish has no cochlea, no endocochlear potential and no outer hair cell amplifier. The mammalian evidence is expression and immunolocalisation only - Stx4a is present through the mouse inner ear and STX4A sits in the cell body, membrane and stereocilia of inner and outer hair cells - and expression is not function. No mouse with an inner ear Stx4 deletion has been reported, and a constitutive knockout would be confounded by the gene's roles elsewhere.
Filed as a human-model mismatch rather than a knowledge gap because the experiment was done, in a model whose fidelity to the human cochlea is the open question, rather than not done at all.

evidence.snippet: Deletions identified in three BMD patients are shown to maintain the translational ORF for amino acids and predict a shorter, lower molecular weight protein.
evidence.explanation: The original statement of the reading-frame model, on the Becker side of the comparison.

evidence.snippet: Ten per cent of patients carried out-of-frame mutations, 4% nonsense mutations and 86% in-frame deletions/duplications.
evidence.explanation: The mutational composition of a 943-patient Becker cohort. It gives both the dominant in-frame class and the size of the exception to the rule.

evidence.snippet: Patients carrying del45-49 compared with del45-47 were associated with an earlier loss of ambulation (P = 1 × 10-4), whereas patients with del45-55 (P = 0.005), del48 (P = 0.02) and del48-49 (P = 0.02) were correlated with a later loss of ambulation compared with del45-47.
evidence.explanation: Within-class genotype-phenotype resolution: which exons are removed changes the trajectory even when the frame is preserved throughout.

steps/1.description: Pathogenic variants in DMD alter dystrophin quantity or function. In-frame deletions and duplications are common, but neither reading frame nor variant position alone establishes the Becker phenotype. The Italian cohort included 779 in-frame, 89 out-of-frame, and 35 nonsense variants among 903 genetically characterized patients. Particular exon deletions correlate with clinical outcomes at the group level; substantial variation remains within genotypes and families.

evidence.snippet: For cases with a deletion mutation, the "reading frame" hypothesis predicts that BMD patients produce a semifunctional, internally deleted dystrophin protein, whereas DMD patients produce a severely truncated protein that would be unstable.
evidence.explanation: The contrast at protein level between the two diseases, which is what this node models.

evidence.snippet: In Becker patients, in-frame mutations allow the synthesis of internally deleted, but largely functional dystrophins.
evidence.explanation: Restatement of the same protein-level claim by a group curating the mutation database.

evidence.snippet: Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked neuromuscular disease attributable to mutations in DMD, leading to a deficient and less functional dystrophin, mainly in skeletal and cardiac muscle.
evidence.explanation: States both the protein state and the two tissues it matters in, which is where this node branches.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly we see reduced dystrophin protein, but not mRNA, in bmx skeletal and cardiac muscle.
evidence.explanation: The exon 45-47 mouse model demonstrates a protein deficit without a corresponding transcript deficit.

evidence.snippet: bmx muscles showed complete loss of nNOS localization at the sarcolemma as did dystrophin‐null mdx52 muscles (Figure 6C).
evidence.explanation: Loss of membrane nNOS is demonstrated for the exon 45-47 model, rather than asserted across all Becker genotypes.

steps/2.description: Residual dystrophin distinguishes the Becker phenotype from severe dystrophin deficiency, but its abundance and function vary. Internally deleted dystrophin is a common outcome, not the only one. In bmx mice with deletion of Dmd exons 45-47, skeletal and cardiac dystrophin protein is reduced despite preserved transcript abundance. Sarcolemmal nNOS localization is lost and alpha-sarcoglycan localization is reduced in this model; these allele-specific observations should not be assumed for every Becker variant.

evidence.snippet: Sarcolemmal staining for nNOS was absent in seven BMD patients (including all five patients with deletion of exons 45–47 or 45–48, and both patients with deletion of exons 3–7) but present in the other six patients.
evidence.explanation: Human biopsies show genotype-associated variation in nNOS localization; membrane loss is not universal in Becker muscular dystrophy.

steps/3.description: Dystrophin serves as a scaffold for sarcolemmal nNOS. Some Becker variants reduce or abolish membrane nNOS localization; other variants retain it. In a biopsy-linked human series, nNOS staining was absent in seven patients and present in six. Total nNOS abundance and residual localization also vary, including between relatives with the same splice variant.

evidence.snippet: Cytosolic NO production correlated with both hypernitrosylation of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium-release-channel ryanodine receptor type-1 (RyR1) and release of calstabin-1, a central hub of Ca(2+) signaling and contraction in muscle.
evidence.explanation: The 12-patient del45-55 biopsy study reports correlated biochemical abnormalities; it does not establish a universal lesion or directly measure the contribution to clinical decline.

steps/4.description: In a study of 12 Becker patients with exon 45-55 deletions, cytosolic nitric oxide production correlated with RyR1 hypernitrosylation and calstabin-1 dissociation. These findings implicate altered regulation of the sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium-release complex. The association does not establish measured calcium leak or its causal contribution across Becker genotypes.

evidence.snippet: This gene codes for dystrophin, a protein important for maintaining the stability of muscle-fiber membranes.
evidence.explanation: Dystrophin's function at the muscle-fibre membrane, which is what a semifunctional protein partly preserves.

evidence.snippet: Ten eccentric contractions of WT EDL muscle resulted in a 15.53% drop in ex vivo peak force. In contrast, this protocol reduced peak force by 20.16% in bmx EDL muscles (P = 0.0239 bmx vs. WT) and 20.86% in mdx EDL (Figure 2D).
evidence.explanation: The genotype-defined model has greater contraction-induced force loss than wild type; it does not establish a uniform degree of protection relative to dystrophin-null muscle.

steps/5.description: Dystrophin supports muscle membrane stability. In Becker muscular dystrophy, residual protein does not fully prevent contraction-related injury. Exon 45-47 bmx mouse muscle shows increased force loss after eccentric contractions, raised serum creatine kinase, necrotic and inflammatory foci, regeneration, and fibrosis. The severity of individual measurements need not lie uniformly between wild type and dystrophin-null muscle.

evidence.snippet: Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked neuromuscular disease attributable to mutations in DMD, leading to a deficient and less functional dystrophin, mainly in skeletal and cardiac muscle.
evidence.explanation: Names cardiac muscle as one of the two tissues carrying the dystrophin deficit, which is the insult this node models.

steps/6.description: Abnormal or reduced dystrophin affects cardiac as well as skeletal muscle. Cardiac disease can progress independently of skeletal muscle severity. The bmx mouse demonstrates reduced cardiac dystrophin and impaired ventricular function; human surveillance must therefore consider the heart even when skeletal weakness is mild.

evidence.snippet: At the histological level, TMEM65 notably displayed a larger distribution and mislocalization from the ICD in both BMD and DMD ventricles
evidence.explanation: Immunostaining shows mislocalization in the rat model; reduced Tmem65 RNA did not correspond to reduced TMEM65 protein abundance in Becker rat hearts.

evidence.snippet: we found that Cx43 was more internalized in both BMD and DMD, with a lower co-localization with N-cadherin (NCAD), an intercalated disc marker
evidence.explanation: Connexin-43 localization changes accompany intercalated-disc disorganization in dystrophic rat hearts.

steps/7.description: In exon 45-47 Becker rats, TMEM65 and connexin-43 are mislocalized and intercalated discs have widened, irregular folds and abnormal contacts with nearby sarcomeres. These findings suggest impaired cardiomyocyte coupling, but no targeted rescue experiment establishes their mediation of ventricular dysfunction. This is model-derived evidence, not a demonstrated universal human cellular lesion.

evidence.snippet: Sympatholysis was greatly impaired in all seven patients lacking sarcolemmal nNOS but well preserved in four of six patients in whom nNOS was detected at the sarcolemma.
evidence.explanation: The biopsy-linked physiology associates loss of sarcolemmal nNOS with impaired exercise vasomodulation, with additional heterogeneity among those retaining nNOS.

evidence.snippet: The key finding of our study is that tadalafil alleviated microvascular ischemia and fully restored blood flow regulation in eight of nine BMD patients who lacked sympatholysis when given placebo.
evidence.explanation: The randomized crossover trial demonstrates an acute physiological response in the subgroup with abnormal placebo physiology, rather than long-term clinical benefit.

evidence.snippet: In the subsequent placebo‐controlled trial performed in six of the 11 patients from the open‐label trial (P2, P3, P7, P12, P14 and P16), we confirmed that sodium nitrate restores functional sympatholysis, whereas placebo was without effect
evidence.explanation: The small randomized crossover substudy confirms an acute vascular response after nitrate supplementation.

steps/8.description: During exercise, affected muscle may fail to attenuate reflex sympathetic vasoconstriction, causing functional ischemia under experimental conditions. This abnormality is associated with nNOS membrane localization but is not present in every Becker patient. Acute tadalafil or nitrate studies demonstrate reversibility of the vascular response; its contribution to chronic weakness or disease progression remains unresolved. Reduced local NO-cGMP signaling is supported by the localization findings and pharmacological rescue rather than by a direct assay of intracellular cGMP in these patients.

evidence.snippet: Information about LoA was known for 822 (87.2%) patients; of these, 111 (13.5%) patients had lost the ability to walk at the time of data collection, with a mean age at LoA of 35.3 (±15.0) years
evidence.explanation: The full cohort report supplies the assessed denominator and observed event age, avoiding interpretation of a cross-sectional fraction as lifetime risk.

evidence.snippet: In 55% of patients, the diagnosis was prompted by the incidental finding of hyperCKaemia.
evidence.explanation: Incidental hyperCKaemia prompted many diagnoses in this Italian cohort; local testing practices affect the proportion.

evidence.snippet: We analysed 190 pulmonary function measurements with a median interval of one year (1-17y) and measured a 1.00% decline of Forced Vital Capacity percent predicted (FVC%pred) per year (p = 0.004).
evidence.explanation: The quantified rate of respiratory decline.

evidence.snippet: However, this decline is significantly more rapid and clinically relevant after loss of ambulation, which warrants a more vigilant follow-up of respiratory function in this subgroup.
evidence.explanation: The interaction with ambulatory status and the surveillance recommendation that follows from it.

steps/9.description: Proximal weakness and mobility loss progress at variable rates. In the retrospective Italian cohort, 111 of 822 patients with available ambulation information had lost walking ability at assessment. The Kaplan-Meier median age at loss of ambulation was 69 years, whereas the observed mean age among those who had already lost ambulation was 35.3 years. These are different statistics; neither describes an inevitable course for an individual. Respiratory decline can become clinically important, especially after loss of ambulation, and warrants surveillance.

evidence.snippet: One hundred and eighty-seven (30.1%) patients showed LVEF% of <55%
evidence.explanation: The full text defines the cardiac outcome as reduced ejection fraction and supplies its numerator; 621 patients had an LVEF measurement.

evidence.snippet: Both del45-55 (P = 0.002) and del48 (P = 0.003) were significantly associated with decreased odds of developing a pathological left ventricular ejection fraction compared with del45-47.
evidence.explanation: Genotypic modulation of the cardiac endpoint within the in-frame class.

evidence.snippet: Despite the milder skeletal muscle involvement, heart failure from DCM is a common cause of morbidity and the most common cause of death in BMD. Mean age of death is in the mid-40s.
evidence.explanation: The older GeneReviews abstract identifies heart failure as a major source of morbidity and mortality. Its summary age at death is not compared numerically with ambulation estimates from another cohort.

steps/10.description: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction and dilated cardiomyopathy are important complications, and heart failure is a major cause of mortality. In the Italian cohort, 187 of 621 assessed patients had LVEF below 55%, which measures systolic impairment rather than the prevalence of dilated cardiomyopathy. Certain deletions were associated with lower odds of impaired LVEF, but genotype does not determine an individual outcome.

evidence.snippet: In 55% of patients, the diagnosis was prompted by the incidental finding of hyperCKaemia.
evidence.explanation: Raised creatine kinase as the presenting finding in the majority. The frequency slot is left empty because 55% describes how the diagnosis was prompted, not how many patients have a raised CK.

steps/11.description: Raised serum creatine kinase can precede recognized weakness and may prompt incidental diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: More moderate skeletal muscle manifestations (e.g., BMD) may be characterized by onset in adolescence to adulthood of progressive symmetric muscle weakness (proximal > distal) often with calf hypertrophy; weakness of quadriceps femoris (sometimes the only sign); activity-induced cramping (present in some individuals); preservation of neck flexor muscle strength; and flexion contractures of the elbows (if present, late in the course).
evidence.explanation: The Becker-specific clinical paragraph supports the proximal distribution and progressive course.

evidence.snippet: One hundred and eighty-seven (30.1%) patients showed LVEF% of <55%
evidence.explanation: The full text defines the cardiac outcome as reduced ejection fraction and supplies its numerator; 621 patients had an LVEF measurement.

steps/13.description: Reduced left ventricular systolic function was present in 187 of 621 assessed patients in the Italian cohort, using LVEF below 55%. Ventricular dilation was not required for this outcome.

evidence.snippet: Despite the milder skeletal muscle involvement, heart failure from DCM is a common cause of morbidity and the most common cause of death in BMD.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews identifies DCM-related heart failure as a common and important Becker phenotype without giving a numeric frequency band.

steps/14.description: Dilated cardiomyopathy and DCM-related heart failure are important Becker cardiac complications.

evidence.snippet: Only 12 patients (2.7%) had FVC% values of <50%, and all of them were non-ambulant
evidence.explanation: The full text defines the respiratory threshold and ambulatory status. The denominator is 441 patients with FVC measurements, not all 943 participants.

steps/15.description: Respiratory muscle impairment may develop, particularly with advanced motor disability. In the Italian cohort, 12 of 441 patients with available measurements had FVC below 50% predicted, and all 12 were nonambulant.

evidence.snippet: This is followed by weakness in standing up or a waddling gait.
evidence.explanation: The guideline describes waddling gait in the progression of lower-limb muscle involvement.

steps/16.description: Pelvic-girdle weakness can produce a waddling gait.

evidence.snippet: Axial weakness: scoliosis, abdominal weakness with difficulties in getting up from the lying position
evidence.explanation: The neuromuscular assessment section lists scoliosis among manifestations of axial weakness.

steps/17.description: Scoliosis can accompany axial weakness and requires musculoskeletal assessment.

evidence.snippet: Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked neuromuscular disease attributable to mutations in DMD, leading to a deficient and less functional dystrophin, mainly in skeletal and cardiac muscle.
evidence.explanation: The cohort report connects DMD mutations to the partly functional dystrophin state in skeletal and cardiac muscle.

edges/1.description: DMD variants can produce reduced amounts of dystrophin, an abnormal protein, or both, while retaining sufficient function for a Becker clinical phenotype. The protein outcome cannot be inferred solely from reading-frame preservation.

evidence.snippet: Ten eccentric contractions of WT EDL muscle resulted in a 15.53% drop in ex vivo peak force. In contrast, this protocol reduced peak force by 20.16% in bmx EDL muscles (P = 0.0239 bmx vs. WT) and 20.86% in mdx EDL (Figure 2D).
evidence.explanation: The genotype-defined model has greater contraction-induced force loss than wild type; it does not establish a uniform degree of protection relative to dystrophin-null muscle.

edges/2.description: Partly functional dystrophin provides incomplete protection against contraction-induced skeletal muscle injury. The exon 45-47 bmx model retains susceptibility to eccentric contractions.

evidence.snippet: Specifically, bmx mice show deficits in muscle and cardiac function, reduced dystrophin protein in skeletal and cardiac muscle, and histopathology consistent with moderate dystrophy.
evidence.explanation: The bmx model connects the Dmd lesion and reduced cardiac dystrophin with cardiac dysfunction; detailed cellular intermediates are not resolved by this summary.

edges/3.description: The dystrophin deficit also affects cardiomyocytes and can cause cardiac dysfunction despite relatively preserved skeletal muscle function.

evidence.snippet: Sarcolemmal staining for nNOS was absent in seven BMD patients (including all five patients with deletion of exons 45–47 or 45–48, and both patients with deletion of exons 3–7) but present in the other six patients.
evidence.explanation: Human biopsies show genotype-associated variation in nNOS localization; membrane loss is not universal in Becker muscular dystrophy.

edges/4.description: Some DMD variants disrupt dystrophin-dependent membrane localization of nNOS. Human biopsy evidence shows this for several exon-deletion groups, while other Becker variants retain sarcolemmal nNOS.

evidence.snippet: In the early stages BMD involves active myonecrosis and regeneration; later in the disease course chronic myopathic changes are more likely, including increased skeletal muscle fiber size variability, fibrosis, and fat replacement of muscle tissue
evidence.explanation: The trial introduction summarizes the pathological sequence underlying progressive myopathy; it is a literature synthesis, not a longitudinal histology result of this trial.

edges/5.description: Recurrent injury, degeneration, and fibrofatty replacement contribute to progressive loss of skeletal muscle function; the pace varies across patients.

evidence.snippet: For adults with BMD, serum biomarkers of muscle injury trended down progressively with sevasemten treatment (average maximal reductions of 70% for creatine kinase, 98% for fast skeletal muscle troponin I, and 45% for myoglobin).
evidence.explanation: This Becker-specific trial identifies circulating CK as a muscle-injury biomarker. The small biomarker study does not establish a clinical treatment benefit or a direct measure of strength.

evidence.snippet: The increase in CK levels is more marked at the beginning of the di sease and progressively decreases with muscle fatty in volution.
evidence.explanation: The Becker guideline explains why a lower CK level can accompany loss of muscle tissue rather than improved muscle function.

edges/6.description: Circulating creatine kinase is a marker of skeletal muscle injury in Becker muscular dystrophy. Its level does not directly measure remaining strength and can decline as muscle is replaced by fat.

evidence.snippet: More moderate skeletal muscle manifestations (e.g., BMD) may be characterized by onset in adolescence to adulthood of progressive symmetric muscle weakness (proximal > distal) often with calf hypertrophy; weakness of quadriceps femoris (sometimes the only sign); activity-induced cramping (present in some individuals); preservation of neck flexor muscle strength;
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews describes the proximal distribution, progression, and activity-related symptoms of Becker myopathy.

edges/7.description: Proximal weakness is the principal clinical manifestation of the skeletal myopathy.

evidence.snippet: This is followed by weakness in standing up or a waddling gait.
evidence.explanation: The Becker clinical sequence links progressive lower-limb impairment with the gait abnormality.

edges/8.description: Pelvic-girdle involvement alters gait as weakness progresses.

evidence.snippet: Axial weakness: scoliosis, abdominal weakness with difficulties in getting up from the lying position
evidence.explanation: The guideline lists scoliosis as a manifestation associated with axial weakness.

edges/9.description: Axial muscle weakness can contribute to scoliosis.

evidence.snippet: BMD patients may experience progressive deterioration in their respiratory function related to a decrease in the strength of respiratory muscles
evidence.explanation: The respiratory section explicitly links functional deterioration to respiratory muscle weakness.

edges/10.description: Extension of muscle weakness to respiratory muscles can reduce ventilatory capacity.

evidence.snippet: BMD rats exhibit moderate damage to locomotor and diaphragmatic muscles but suffer from a progressive cardiomyopathy.
evidence.explanation: The Dmd exon-deletion model develops progressive cardiomyopathy, without identifying all intervening injury and remodeling steps.

edges/11.description: Cardiac dystrophin dysfunction can lead to progressive ventricular impairment. The exon 45-47 rat model supports progression to cardiomyopathy, while the intervening cellular sequence is not fully established for human Becker disease.

evidence.snippet: At the histological level, TMEM65 notably displayed a larger distribution and mislocalization from the ICD in both BMD and DMD ventricles
evidence.explanation: Immunostaining shows mislocalization in the rat model; reduced Tmem65 RNA did not correspond to reduced TMEM65 protein abundance in Becker rat hearts.

edges/12.description: The exon 45-47 rat model shows altered intercalated-disc architecture and protein localization. The contribution of dystrophin quantity versus its altered structure is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: One hundred and eighty-seven (30.1%) patients showed LVEF% of <55%
evidence.explanation: The full text defines the cardiac outcome as reduced ejection fraction and supplies its numerator; 621 patients had an LVEF measurement.

edges/13.description: Reduced LVEF is the clinical readout of ventricular systolic dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: Despite the milder skeletal muscle involvement, heart failure from DCM is a common cause of morbidity and the most common cause of death in BMD.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews identifies DCM-related heart failure as a major Becker outcome.

edges/14.description: Becker ventricular disease can progress to dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.

evidence.snippet: We propose that disruption in the localization of TMEM65 and Cx43 could play a role in altering electrical synchronization during myocardial depolarization or repolarization, due to partly inefficient intercellular communications.
evidence.explanation: The authors explicitly frame this mechanism as a proposal; the edge retains that uncertainty.

edges/15.description: Altered mechanical and electrical coupling is a proposed contributor to cardiac dysfunction in the rat model. Co-occurrence and structural data support the hypothesis, while causal mediation remains untested.

evidence.snippet: Sympatholysis was greatly impaired in all seven patients lacking sarcolemmal nNOS but well preserved in four of six patients in whom nNOS was detected at the sarcolemma.
evidence.explanation: The biopsy-linked physiology associates loss of sarcolemmal nNOS with impaired exercise vasomodulation, with additional heterogeneity among those retaining nNOS.

evidence.snippet: The key finding of our study is that tadalafil alleviated microvascular ischemia and fully restored blood flow regulation in eight of nine BMD patients who lacked sympatholysis when given placebo.
evidence.explanation: The randomized crossover trial demonstrates an acute physiological response in the subgroup with abnormal placebo physiology, rather than long-term clinical benefit.

evidence.snippet: In the subsequent placebo‐controlled trial performed in six of the 11 patients from the open‐label trial (P2, P3, P7, P12, P14 and P16), we confirmed that sodium nitrate restores functional sympatholysis, whereas placebo was without effect
evidence.explanation: The small randomized crossover substudy confirms an acute vascular response after nitrate supplementation.

edges/16.description: Loss of membrane-associated nNOS weakens local nitric-oxide-dependent attenuation of sympathetic vasoconstriction during exercise. Acute rescue with interventions that augment NO-cGMP signaling supports this pathway, without proving an effect on long-term muscle decline.

evidence.snippet: Cytosolic NO production correlated with both hypernitrosylation of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium-release-channel ryanodine receptor type-1 (RyR1) and release of calstabin-1, a central hub of Ca(2+) signaling and contraction in muscle.
evidence.explanation: The 12-patient del45-55 biopsy study reports correlated biochemical abnormalities; it does not establish a universal lesion or directly measure the contribution to clinical decline.

edges/17.description: Mislocalized cytosolic nNOS is associated with altered RyR1-calstabin regulation in del45-55 muscle biopsies. The human study supports a candidate nitrosative pathway but does not resolve causal mediation or establish this branch for every Becker variant.

evidence.snippet: About 60% of both Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) and Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is due to deletions of the dystrophin gene.
evidence.explanation: The historical deletion study establishes the shared DMD locus; it does not establish an absolute reading-frame discriminator.

genes/0.notes: DMD pathogenic variants cause a spectrum of dystrophinopathies. Becker classification integrates the clinical course and residual dystrophin with the molecular result. In-frame changes predominate, but out-of-frame and nonsense variants are established exceptions; reading frame alone is insufficient for diagnosis or individual prognosis.

evidence.snippet: Thus, there is no indication to use ACE inhibitors for systematic treatment of BMD patients regardless of cardiac phenotype, such as in Duchenne MD.
evidence.explanation: The French guideline does not support universal ACE-inhibitor prophylaxis irrespective of the Becker cardiac phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Patients with LVEF < 50% and/or evidence of myocardial fibrosis on MRI should be referre d to a specialized cardiologist in a tertiary center to discuss the  initiation of cardioprotective
evidence.explanation: Reduced LVEF or myocardial fibrosis prompts specialist assessment of cardioprotective treatment in this guideline.

treatments/0.description: ACE inhibitors are first-line medication for established Becker cardiomyopathy in the 2023 French guideline. That guideline recommends specialist discussion of cardioprotective treatment when LVEF is below 50% or MRI shows myocardial fibrosis. It does not recommend prophylactic ACE inhibition for every Becker patient with normal cardiac findings; evidence from Duchenne muscular dystrophy does not establish that indication in Becker muscular dystrophy.

evidence.snippet: ACE inhibitors are used with or without beta blockers for cardiomyopathy in both DMD and BMD phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: The indication for established cardiomyopathy in both phenotypes.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Treats ventricular dysfunction and adverse remodeling associated with cardiomyopathy.

evidence.snippet: Corticosteroid therapy improves muscle strength and function for individuals with DMD between ages five and 15 years; the same treatment is used in BMD, although the efficacy is less clear.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews explicitly qualifies the uncertain Becker efficacy while describing clinical use.

evidence.snippet: Out of the 20 participants, seven were female, nineteen had LGMD and one had BMD
evidence.explanation: The mixed pilot cohort contained only one Becker participant, precluding a Becker-specific efficacy estimate.

treatments/1.description: Corticosteroids are used in selected patients with Becker muscular dystrophy, but efficacy is less established than in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Benefits, adverse effects, and treatment duration require individual assessment; Duchenne trial results do not establish Becker efficacy. A 24-week open-label weekly-prednisone pilot enrolled 19 participants with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy and only one with Becker muscular dystrophy; pooled biomarker and functional changes do not establish Becker-specific benefit.

evidence.snippet: In patients with terminal heart failure who have lost ambulation or have significant respiratory failure, cardi ac transplantati on is generally not indicated
evidence.explanation: The guideline identifies motor and respiratory impairment as constraints on transplant selection.

treatments/2.description: Cardiac transplantation may be considered for terminal heart failure in selected patients with limited skeletal muscle disability and without severe respiratory failure. Selection requires multidisciplinary assessment. The French guideline generally does not recommend transplantation after loss of ambulation or with significant respiratory failure; ventricular assist devices can be discussed individually in expert centers.

evidence.snippet: cardiac transplantation is offered to persons with severe dilated cardiomyopathy and BMD with limited or no clinical evidence of skeletal muscle disease.
evidence.explanation: The indication and its selection criterion.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Replaces the failing heart while leaving the underlying DMD variant and extracardiac manifestations unchanged.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac monitoring must systematically include ECG and echocardiogram. The other examinations must be discussed with the patient on the basis of the patients’ symptoms and ECG and echocardiogram findings. The frequency of these assessments depends on the initial findings. The minimum interval for a classic form of B MD with a normal echocardiogram is two years.
evidence.explanation: The Becker guideline specifies ECG and echocardiography and a two-year interval when the echocardiogram is normal.

evidence.snippet: For patie nts with LVEF < 50%, monitoring should be performed at least once a year.
evidence.explanation: Ventricular dysfunction calls for more frequent assessment.

evidence.snippet: DMD/BMD By cardiologist incl EKG & echocardiogram or cardiac MRI • Annually & before major surgery • More frequently in those age >10 yrs & those w/myocardial fibrosis or ventricular dysfunction
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews Table 8 recommends annual and preoperative cardiac assessment; its footnote identifies Duchenne care guidelines as a basis for the intensified schedule.

evidence.snippet: In those without cardiac manifestations, cardiac evaluation with an EKG and cardiac imaging every three to five years beginning in the second to third decade of life is recommended.
evidence.explanation: The updated chapter recommends recurring surveillance for heterozygous females with normal initial cardiac findings.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac MRI should also be discussed at diagnosis since it prov ides a more accurate estimation of cardiac function than echocardiography and can identify myocardial fibrosis, ma inly in the inferolateral wall, which can be present in patient s with a normal echocardiogram.
evidence.explanation: MRI can detect myocardial fibrosis despite a normal echocardiogram.

evidence.snippet: In cases showing abnormal cardiac systolic function (left ventricular ejection fraction below 50%) or significant conduction defects on the ECG, a 24-h Holter ECG sho uld also be performed to search for ventricular or supraventricular arrhythmias
evidence.explanation: Abnormal ventricular function or significant conduction defects warrant ambulatory rhythm assessment.

treatments/3.description: Cardiac surveillance starts at diagnosis and continues regardless of skeletal muscle severity. Assessment includes ECG and echocardiography, with cardiac MRI to assess fibrosis and function when appropriate and Holter monitoring for cardiac dysfunction or conduction abnormalities. The 2026 GeneReviews chapter lists annual cardiac assessment for affected males and assessment before major surgery, with closer monitoring for fibrosis or dysfunction; its schedule partly draws on Duchenne care guidance. The 2023 French Becker guideline proposes assessment every two years with a normal echocardiogram and at least annually with LVEF below 50%. The interval should be individualized by cardiology. GeneReviews recommends ECG and cardiac imaging every three to five years for heterozygous females without cardiac manifestations, beginning in the second to third decade, and specialist-directed follow-up when abnormalities are present.

evidence.snippet: AIR seems to be a specific complication of general anaesthesia in dystrophinopathies, especially at paediatric age. AIR can cause life‐threatening hyperkalaemia, and the risk of occurrence is possibly linked to the use of succinylcholine and/or volatile anaesthetics
evidence.explanation: The muscular-dystrophy recommendations identify anaesthesia-induced rhabdomyolysis and hyperkalaemia as the relevant dystrophinopathy hazards.

evidence.snippet: There is no association with MH
evidence.explanation: In Table 4, this statement follows the dystrophinopathy AIR recommendation and distinguishes it from malignant hyperthermia; it does not remove the need for anaesthetic precautions.

treatments/4.description: Preoperative planning should assess cardiac and respiratory involvement and muscle weakness. Avoid succinylcholine because of hyperkalaemia and rhabdomyolysis risk. Volatile anaesthetics also require specialist risk assessment because of anaesthesia-induced rhabdomyolysis in dystrophinopathies. The ENMC consensus distinguishes this complication from malignant hyperthermia and reports no association of dystrophinopathies with malignant hyperthermia susceptibility.

evidence.snippet: The study failed to achieve the primary endpoint. However, there was a potential signal from the MRI assessments suggesting givinostat could prevent (or slow down) BMD disease progression.
evidence.explanation: The trial conclusion distinguishes the negative primary outcome from the exploratory interpretation of secondary MRI findings.

evidence.snippet: Adverse events, most mild or moderate, were reported by 88.2% and 52.9% patients receiving givinostat and placebo.
evidence.explanation: Adverse events were more frequent with givinostat; the paper details platelet and triglyceride abnormalities.

treatments/5.description: A 12-month placebo-controlled trial in 51 adults with Becker muscular dystrophy failed its primary total-fibrosis endpoint and showed no significant functional benefit. Secondary thigh and quadriceps MRI fat-fraction findings suggested a possible signal, but baseline imbalance and the small sample limit interpretation. This is investigational Becker evidence and does not establish an effective disease-modifying treatment.

evidence.snippet: In Part C, 7 men with BMD were randomized to sevasemten (N = 5) or placebo (N = 2)
evidence.explanation: Defines the very small Becker randomized cohort within a larger study dominated by healthy volunteers.

evidence.snippet: As this was an open-label trial with no placebo control, caution is required in interpretation. Additional limitations of this study include the small sample size and the lack of diversity in enrolled participants (100% White).
evidence.explanation: The 24-month study cannot distinguish treatment benefit from natural-history variability or other uncontrolled influences.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with sevasemten was associated with reductions in circulating biomarkers of muscle injury that were evident within 4 weeks and sustained for up to 24 months. Physical function, as assessed by North Star Ambulatory Assessment (NSAA), was stable over 24 months.
evidence.explanation: Records the observed biomarker and functional trajectories without treating them as randomized efficacy evidence.

treatments/6.description: Sevasemten inhibits fast skeletal muscle myosin ATPase to reduce injurious contraction. A short phase 1 Becker cohort comprised five treated patients and two placebo recipients; muscle-injury biomarkers decreased but the study was too small and short to establish clinical efficacy. In a later uncontrolled 12-person study, biomarkers remained reduced and functional measures were stable over two years. These observations support investigation, not a proven treatment effect. The completed CANYON/GRAND CANYON registry had no posted results at the September 2026 review.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with sevasemten was associated with reductions in circulating biomarkers of muscle injury that were evident within 4 weeks and sustained for up to 24 months.
evidence.explanation: The 12-person study reports a durable biomarker association consistent with the proposed target effect, with no placebo control to establish efficacy.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: Investigational fast-myosin inhibition aims to reduce contraction-associated muscle injury. Sustained biomarker reductions in the small open-label Becker study support this proposed effect; they do not establish prevention of long-term functional decline.

evidence.snippet: Dystrophin increases of 49% (p < 0.0001) were found in the gastrocnemius and 55% (p = 0.0173) in the heart with vamorolone treatment
evidence.explanation: The mouse experiment shows an increase relative to vehicle-treated bmx animals, not normalization to healthy dystrophin levels or proof of human efficacy.

evidence.snippet: to fully demonstrate causation, further studies are needed to expand upon these and previous studies.
evidence.explanation: The authors limit the proposed microRNA mechanism: reduced microRNAs and increased dystrophin correlate, but direct causal mediation was not demonstrated.

treatments/7.description: Vamorolone improved selected strength and histological measures and increased dystrophin protein in bmx mice. This preclinical study did not establish human efficacy or long-term cardiac benefit. The subsequently completed Becker phase II pilot has registry results posted in September 2026; its 24-week functional data are descriptive and do not establish a clinically meaningful benefit. The trial must be distinguished from Duchenne treatment evidence.

evidence.snippet: This physical activity must be gentle and progressive and must take into account the specificities of BMD when choosing the exercises to offer
evidence.explanation: The guideline recommends gradual activity adapted to Becker muscular dystrophy.

evidence.snippet: Maintenance of segmenta l and spinal muscular and joint flexibility for analgesic pu rposes by passive mobilizations and stretching, prepar ation and recovery for exercise and proprioceptive stimulation: stretching, posture, etc.
evidence.explanation: Stretching and passive mobilization address flexibility and discomfort.

evidence.snippet: The most affected muscl es (those with a muscle testing MRC rating < 4) require more precautions, specifically by limiting intense contract ions and eccentric stresses and promoting aerobic metabolism.
evidence.explanation: Weak muscles require limits on intense contraction and eccentric loading.

treatments/8.description: Individualized physical therapy uses gentle progressive aerobic activity, stretching, low-resistance exercise, balance work, and fall prevention to maintain function and joint mobility. Exercise intensity should account for muscle weakness, fatigue, pain, and cardiac or respiratory involvement; avoid excessive contraction and eccentric loading of weak muscles.

evidence.snippet: Posture orthoses may be used in some patients. In the lower limbs, nocturnal posture orthoses can be proposed to address certain deformities (e.g., anti-flexum knee or antiequine orthosis).
evidence.explanation: Night-time postural orthoses are options for selected deformities.

evidence.snippet: Manual wheelchair; electric scooter and/or electric wh eelchair are necessary when the risks linked to walking (falls, fractures) become greater than the functional benefits.
evidence.explanation: The mobility decision balances walking benefit against injury risk.

evidence.snippet: Specific devices facilitating meals, washing, toileting, leisur e, transfers, and environmental control can be implemented.
evidence.explanation: Assistive devices support daily activities and environmental access.

treatments/9.description: Selected posture or walking orthoses can address deformity and support function. Wheelchairs or scooters become appropriate when walking-related falls and fractures outweigh functional benefit. Occupational and rehabilitation teams can adapt transfers, self-care, communication, and home, school, or workplace access.

evidence.snippet: Some surgeries (e.g., Achilles tendon tenotomy, gastrocnemius aponeurotomy, tendon transfers, osteotomies or foot arthrodesis) are useful, and their u ses must be linked to functions such as walking and posture s tability. Vertebral arthrodesis is limited to the most severe forms close to DMD
evidence.explanation: The guideline links surgery to functional impairment and limits spinal fusion to severe disease.

evidence.snippet: In rare cases, macroglossia surgery may be required because of functional consequences (ventilation, swallowing, etc.).
evidence.explanation: Functionally significant macroglossia is a rare surgical indication.

treatments/10.description: Selected tendon or foot procedures may help walking and posture. Spinal fusion is reserved for severe forms. Rarely, macroglossia with ventilatory or swallowing consequences warrants surgery; operative planning requires cardiac, respiratory, and anesthetic assessment.

evidence.snippet: Cognitive or psychiatric assessment has to be consider ed at diagnosis, and especially in the event of integration or access to employment issues.
evidence.explanation: Assessment is considered from diagnosis and when participation difficulties arise.

evidence.snippet: For children, assessments should be performed every 2 –3 years to monitor a child’s developmental progress and response to interventions.
evidence.explanation: Repeated childhood assessment guides developmental support.

evidence.snippet: Formal annual evaluation by the mental health clinician is advised to assess the psychological wellbeing of the individual, parents, and siblings.
evidence.explanation: The guideline includes recurring psychological evaluation for patients and families.

evidence.snippet: Depending on the patient’s age and disease status, it may be necessary to pay special att ention to their cardiac status, potential medication inte ractions, and side effects when combined with existing medications (e.g., weight gain).
evidence.explanation: Psychotropic treatment requires attention to comorbidity and concomitant medication.

treatments/11.description: Assess cognitive, educational, behavioral, and emotional needs from diagnosis and when school or employment difficulties emerge. Use findings to tailor family, school, and workplace support. The French guideline recommends reassessment every two to three years in children, mental-health screening at neuromuscular visits, and formal annual psychological evaluation. Medication decisions should account for cardiac status, interactions, and adverse effects.

evidence.snippet: A respiratory functional exploration should be performed every 2 years, with no pulmonologist advice required at this stage if the findings are normal.
evidence.explanation: The French guideline gives a two-year interval when respiratory testing is normal.

evidence.snippet: In cases with an abnormal fVC, the frequency of monitoring should be ann ual. A subsequent pulmonologist assessment, performed a t least annually, will indicate the need for blood gas analysis or nightly examinations.
evidence.explanation: Abnormal FVC warrants annual or more frequent specialist assessment.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory By pulmonologist for assessment of respiratory function Annually; then every 6 mos after loss of ambulation
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews Table 8 gives a more frequent dystrophinopathy schedule; footnote 1 identifies its Duchenne guideline basis.

treatments/12.description: Regular evaluation includes symptoms of nocturnal hypoventilation, orthopnea, cough effectiveness, pulmonary function, and sleep investigations when indicated. The French Becker guideline recommends pulmonary function testing every two years if normal and annual specialist follow-up if abnormal. The 2026 GeneReviews dystrophinopathy schedule recommends annual respiratory evaluation and every six months after loss of ambulation, citing Duchenne care guidance. The treating team should individualize frequency to findings and progression.

evidence.snippet: In cases showing actual diaphragmatic involvemen t with hypoventilation, nocturn al noninvasive ventilation will be offered by the pulmonologist with a specific followup.
evidence.explanation: The guideline links nocturnal noninvasive ventilation to documented hypoventilation.

treatments/13.description: Nocturnal noninvasive ventilation is offered when diaphragmatic weakness produces hypoventilation, with specialist titration and follow-up. Respiratory support depends on functional assessment and symptoms rather than skeletal muscle disability alone.

evidence.snippet: In cases showing a cough d eficiency, cough aid techniques will be offered by the pulmonologist or physiotherapist. A pulmonologist follow-up is then necessary.
evidence.explanation: The guideline recommends cough assistance when a cough deficit is present.

treatments/14.description: Weak or ineffective cough warrants respiratory physiotherapy and individually selected manual or mechanical cough-assistance techniques, with pulmonology follow-up.

evidence.snippet: If the disorders are secondary to poor pharyngeal propulsion, the textures (mixed, adequately “slippery”) of the food and the po sition of the head during meals should be adapted.
evidence.explanation: Food texture and head position are adapted to swallowing mechanics.

evidence.snippet: Oral nutritional supplements may be offered when increase in caloric intake becomes necessary.
evidence.explanation: Supplementation is considered when increased caloric intake is needed.

evidence.snippet: In the most severe patien ts there is a risk of secondary undernutrition. It is then necessary to identify all the aggravating factors: involvement of the upper limbs (speci al cutlery, raised meal plan …), macroglossia or involvement of chewing muscles (hygiene care o ral, speech therapy, adaptation of the texture of food, surgery), digestive damage (constipation, …), spinal defo rmities sources of compression, mask ventilation that causes or worsens aerogastria.
evidence.explanation: Nutritional assessment includes feeding mechanics, gastrointestinal problems, deformity, and ventilation-related factors.

treatments/15.description: Assess chewing, swallowing safety, weight trajectory, and nutritional intake. Adapt food texture and head position for impaired pharyngeal propulsion, provide feeding aids and speech-language input as needed, and consider oral nutritional supplements when intake is inadequate. Changes in mobility require reassessment of energy needs.

evidence.snippet: Situations necessitating artificial feeding are rare in patients with BMD. If oral feeding cannot ensure safe nutritive intake, a gastrostomy can be set up as the last resort. However, bef ore creating a gastrostomy, the patient’s respiratory function a nd, in particular, the need for noninvasive ventilation shoul d be evaluated. The gastrostomy should be placed by a team accustomed to the care of disabled patients.
evidence.explanation: The guideline describes the indication and preprocedural respiratory assessment.

open_questions/0.rationale: Some Duchenne exon-skipping therapies restore an open reading frame and aim to produce partly functional, Becker-like dystrophin. Becker natural history and genotype-specific models can inform expectations, but an induced protein is not guaranteed to reproduce a particular Becker clinical trajectory. This untreated disease entry does not assert an antisense intervention in its causal path.

evidence.snippet: The correlation between phenotype and type of deletion mutation is in agreement with the "reading frame" theory in 92% of cases and is of diagnostic and prognostic significance.

evidence.explanation: The ascertainment argument, made by the authors themselves, which bears on how the 92% should be read.

open_questions/1.rationale: Reading-frame concordance is a statistical association: the 1989 deletion series reported 92%, and the Leiden database reported 91%. The Italian Becker cohort separately contained out-of-frame and nonsense variants among clinically characterized patients. These percentages have different denominators and cannot be pooled. Alternative splicing, translational re-initiation, and distal truncation can help explain exceptions, but the rescue mechanism must be demonstrated for the specific variant. Phenotype, dystrophin protein, and molecular findings should be interpreted together. Mild or asymptomatic in-frame deletion carriers may also be underascertained.

evidence.snippet: The c.913C>T variant on the paternal allele is predicted to result in a premature stop codon p.(Gln305*), and likely explains the decreased protein expression observed in myocardial tissue and skin fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Documents reduced GET3/ASNA1 protein in patient heart and fibroblasts attributable to the nonsense allele.

evidence.snippet: 2 variants c.867C>G p.(Cys289Trp) and c.913C>T p.(Gln305*) in cis configuration on the paternal allele, and a missense variant c.488T>C p.(Val163Ala) on the maternal allele
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the paternal allele carries two variants in cis, not one, which the earlier description omitted.

evidence.snippet: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction analysis showed equal amounts of wild-type and mutant products. Hence, no evidence was found for nonsense-mediated decay.
evidence.explanation: A non-obvious negative result given a premature stop codon - the truncated transcript escapes decay, so truncated protein is produced.

steps/1.description: Three variants across two alleles, not two. The paternal allele carries c.867C>G p.(Cys289Trp) and c.913C>T p.(Gln305*) in cis; the maternal allele carries c.488T>C p.(Val163Ala). The cis pairing matters mechanistically: Cys289 is part of an essential zinc-binding site, so the paternal allele is doubly compromised rather than simply truncated. Reduced protein abundance was demonstrated directly in patient myocardium and skin fibroblasts. The maternal missense allele leaves protein present but misfolded. Notably the premature stop codon does not trigger nonsense-mediated decay - wild-type and mutant transcripts were present in equal amounts - so the truncated protein is made.

evidence.snippet: ASNA1 (also known as TRC40 or GET3) serves as the central ATP-dependent chaperone delivering TA proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the specific molecular role that is lost.

steps/2.description: GET3/ASNA1 is the central ATP-dependent chaperone that receives tail-anchored proteins from the BAG6/UBL4A/TRC35 pre-targeting complex and delivers them to the WRB/CAML receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane. Losing it both destabilizes that pre-targeting complex and reduces the expression of multiple tail-anchored substrates. Tail-anchored proteins are roughly 5% of integral membrane proteins, which is why a single chaperone defect has such broad downstream consequences.

evidence.snippet: Transcriptomic analyses revealed compensatory upregulation of genes involved in protein trafficking and Golgi-to-ER transport, reflecting maladaptive responses to disrupted vesicular transport.
evidence.explanation: Documents the disrupted vesicular transport and the maladaptive compensatory response in cardiomyocytes.

steps/3.description: In cardiomyocytes the consequence is disrupted vesicular transport and proteostasis, with compensatory transcriptional upregulation of protein trafficking and Golgi-to-ER transport genes — a maladaptive response rather than a successful rescue.

evidence.snippet: Desmin staining confirmed myofibrillar disorganization
evidence.explanation: Documents myofibrillar disorganization in patient myocardium.

evidence.snippet: Microscopic examination of the myocardium showed prominent subendothelial fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Documents the fibrotic change accompanying the structural disorganization.

steps/4.description: The tissue-level correlate of the trafficking defect, and the step the entry previously asserted without one. Intercalated discs are irregular with increased intercellular space on N-cadherin labelling and electron microscopy, desmin staining shows myofibrillar disorganization, and the myocardium carries prominent subendothelial fibrosis. The authors tie the intercalated disc lesion to the same finding in wrb-deficient models and in phospholamban disease, which is what makes it mechanistically specific rather than a non-specific end-stage change.

evidence.snippet: Loss of asna1 in zebrafish resulted in reduced cardiac contractility and early lethality.

evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing was used to screen for the causative genetic defect in a pair of siblings with rapidly progressive dilated cardiomyopathy and death in early infancy.

edges/11.description: Developed in the dilated, poorly contractile ventricle during ECMO and was refractory to medical therapy.

evidence.snippet: The c.488T>C variant on the maternal allele results in a valine to alanine substitution at residue 163 (p.Val163Ala).
evidence.explanation: Specifies the maternal missense allele in the index sibship.

genes/0.notes: Biallelic variants in GET3 (HGNC-approved symbol; long known as ASNA1 and also called TRC40), encoding the central ATP-dependent targeting factor of the GET/TRC tail-anchored protein insertion pathway. The reported genotype is three variants across two alleles, not two: c.867C>G p.(Cys289Trp) and c.913C>T p.(Gln305*) in cis on the paternal allele, and c.488T>C p.(Val163Ala) on the maternal allele. The cis pairing matters - Cys289 is part of an essential zinc-binding site, so the paternal allele is doubly compromised rather than simply truncated. All three were absent from gnomAD v2.0.2, and the index paper cites a pLI of 0.92 from that release as evidence of loss-of-function intolerance. Treat that number as version-bound: current gnomAD gives a much lower pLI for this gene, so the constraint estimate has moved between releases and only the v2.0.2 value should be attributed to the paper. Note that the entire published human literature uses the ASNA1 symbol.

evidence.snippet: it cannot be excluded that this ASNA1 variant acted as a modifier of the LMNA-related cardiomyopathy

genes/1.notes: A single heterozygous c.547G>A p.(Val183Met) ASNA1 variant was found in an unrelated patient with LMNA-related dilated cardiomyopathy who needed transplantation at 16. In-silico predictors call it tolerated or likely benign and no second allele was found, so this is not a second case of CMD2H. The authors raise it only as a possible modifier of the LMNA disease, and it is recorded here at that strength and no more.
